invocation: MODEL_BACKEND=stub TEAM_SECRET=local-demo-team-secret python3 solution/solve.py  (default: deterministic in-process stub self-test, no live target). Live helper: python3 solution/solve.py --live http://{HOST}:{PORT}
target_details: Default mode (no args) runs stub_test(), which drives the app via Flask's app.test_client() in-process against the imported app module -- no host/port, no network. It requires env MODEL_BACKEND=stub and TEAM_SECRET=local-demo-team-secret (it validates the returned flag against flag.flag('local-demo-team-secret')). The --live mode reads the target URL from argv: sys.argv[1]=='--live' and sys.argv[2]==URL, then POSTs to URL.rstrip('/')+'/chat'. The app itself serves on port 8080 (internal_port 8080). --live is only an interactive stdin helper (input('you> ')), NOT an automated solver.
flag_output: Stub self-test prints the flag (lines 'flag from tool :' and 'flag from flag.py:') and 'ALL CHECKS PASSED'; it raises AssertionError on failure. It does NOT produce a per-team NCTF{...} against a live instance. In --live mode the flag would appear in the printed CUSTODIAN disburse tool-result JSON (key 'flag') once the gate unseals.
dev_flag_fallback: flag.py get_flag() returns NCTF{ CHALLENGE_SECRET[:24] } when FLAG/CHALLENGE_SECRET set; with both unset it derives CHALLENGE_SECRET = HMAC_SHA256(TEAM_SECRET or 'local-dev-secret', 'ai-agent-tool-abuse') and returns NCTF{ that[:24] }. The stub solver instead calls flag.flag('local-demo-team-secret') = NCTF{ HMAC_SHA256('local-demo-team-secret','ai-agent-tool-abuse')[:24] }.
blockers: The default solve.py mode is only a deterministic offline STUB self-test (mechanism proof), NOT a real solve: it forces MODEL_BACKEND=stub and uses Flask's in-process test_client, so it never touches a live instance and only verifies the flag equals the local-dev HMAC derivation. The actual solve is a stored cross-agent prompt injection requiring a live tool-capable LLM (llama3.1:8b via an Ollama backend behind an admission gateway needing OLLAMA_URL + AI_PROXY_TOKEN) to be jailbroken twice; the --live mode is an interactive stdin helper with no automated payload. So there is no automatable end-to-end solver against a served instance -- needs GPU-backed model, external gateway, and manual/iterative jailbreaking.

blockers: Requires a live per-team instance backed by an Ollama server running llama3.1:8b (multi-GB model). Needs the served guard container plus an Ollama sidecar (several-GB one-time model pull; heavy CPU/GPU); external network for image/model pull. Not runnable against static artifacts.
